title: 10,000 balls fell. 3 reached the edges.
0.001 degrees apart. Watch them disagree.
10,000 games of Monty Hall. One choice doubled the wins.
200 birds, no leader. In sync in 7.8 seconds.
30 pendulums, 30 speeds. One line every 30.0 seconds.
Same 512 bars. One sorter did 29x less work.
3 stars, 1 path, 40 laps. The error grew 482x, not a trillion.
9,272 cells vs 351. Same maze, same shortest path.
50,000 sure, or flip for a million? 10,000 players, 0 left.
22 cars, 0 obstacles. The jam appeared at 52 s and rolled backward at 6.0 km/h.
Random cells, exact threshold. 1,000 grids average 59.26%. Theory says 59.27%.
Everyone asked for 30% alike neighbors. They got 75.9%.
Same 0.001 degree nudge. Round table: 0.1 mm apart. Stadium: 1.79 m. That is chaos.
36 cells, 4 rules. Every 30 generations it fires a glider. 50 of them by generation 1,500.
5 states, blank tape. It runs 47,176,870 steps, then halts. The busy beaver.
Same seeds, same rule, one tenth of a degree off. 0 seeds touching vs 658 in 34 arms.
Two formulas for pi. Seven digits: Ramanujan needs 1 term. Leibniz needs 2,886,750.
Same 1 mm shake. On tempo: the spring snaps at push 27. 3% faster: it never gets close.
Same town, same virus, same 10 first cases. 11 contacts a day: 225 cases. 13 a day: 11,397.
Same coin, 2,000 steps. Line: 207 of 10,000 walkers still out. Plane: 3,013.
The better team wins 55% of games and 60.7% of best-of-7 series. Nine in ten needs a best of 163.
1 shuffle: a guesser names 31 of 52 cards. 7 shuffles: 5. Chance: 4.5.
Same 1,008 buses, same 10,000 passengers. On tempo: 5.0 min wait. At random: 10.0 min.
10 chips vs 100, 10,000 players. Fair coin: 866 broke the house. 49% coin: 64.
10,000 sticks dropped on floorboards. 6,350 crossed a line. Estimate of pi: 3.1496.
Same 10,000 rooms of 23 people. Someone shares YOUR birthday: 569 rooms. Any two share one: 4,922.
Same 10,000 balls, 100 bins. One random pick: stacks 78 to 134. Emptier of two picks: 98 to 102.
50 stickers, 1 random per pack. First 40 took 64 packs. Last 10 took 136.
One coin is fair, one never runs past 3. 10,000 runs of 100 flips: 8,102 streaked 6+. Longest: 21.
Count to 1,000: 112 numbers start with 1, 111 with 9. Double 1,000 times: 301 and 45.
Do they arrive together? Round bowl: 3.2 s apart. Curved bowl: 0.000 s apart, every crossing.
Which one flips? Same brick, same spin. Long axis: never. Middle axis: a flip every 6.8 s.
Do ants find the shortest path? Both bridges open: 98% take the short one. Long bridge first: 0%.
Which slide is fastest? The longest one. Curve: 1.0 s. Straight line: 1.2 s.
Can a pendulum stand upside down? Pivot still: falls in 0.43 s. Shaking 40 times a second: stays up.
Two drops, a hair apart. Same magnet? No. Released 0.1 mm apart: purple and red.
Spin a top 3x faster. Does it circle faster? No: 2.0 s a lap became 6.0 s. Same top, same lean.
Know the start 1,000x better. How much longer can you predict? The same 7.5 s each time. Lorenz.
Add more circles. Does the bump go away? 5 circles: 18% too high. 50: 18%. 5,000: 18%. Never.
What is the fastest way to board a plane? Window seats first 5:18, back to front 19:12, 3.6x slower
You wait on floor 2. Which way is the first elevator going? Down, 8,900 times out of 10,000.
One ant, two rules. What does it build? A mess for 9,977 steps, then a highway: 104 steps a block.
Drop a slinky. When does the bottom fall? Not when you let go: when the top hits it, 0.29 s later.
Drop a tennis ball on a basketball. How high does it fly? 5.6 m from a 1 m drop. Alone: 1 m.
Fall through the Earth. How long to the other side? 42 min, via the centre or a 4,000 km tunnel.
Speed up in orbit. Do you pull ahead? No. One lap later the faster ship is 167 km behind.
How does a swing go higher? Stand at the bottom, squat at the top: past 60 degrees in 8 swings.
Why do these two end up ticking together? On a rolling board: in step in 23 s. On the table: never.
Drop one bullet, fire one level. Which lands first? Neither: both hit at 0.553 s, 199 m apart.
Where is the jet when you hear it? At twice the speed of sound: already 173 m past you.
Can a planet throw a ship faster, for free? Pass behind it: +4.1 km/s. In front: -5.1 km/s.
Why is every rainbow the same size? 10,000 rays into one drop pile up at 42.4 degrees, none past it.
Can a ball go through a wall? With 80% of the energy needed, never. 3.2% of a quantum wave gets out.
Push a ball across a spinning record. Where does it go? A circle back to the centre every 3.5 turns.
Which one rolls down first? Same mass, same size: the solid ball in 1.29 s, the hoop last in 1.54 s.
Can a swing pass its motion to its neighbour? Start one at 10 degrees: all of it crosses in 20 s.
Spin the hoop. Where does the bead settle? At 100 turns a minute the bead holds 63.4 degrees up.
Aim straight at it. It drops as you fire. Do you hit? Yes: from 20 m, both fell 2.72 m by the hit.
Turn the tap up. Does the wheel spin faster? No. With 3x the water it reversed 6 times in 4 minutes.
Lift two balls. How many fly out? Two, to 10 cm, and never one ball at double speed.
A one meter wave at sea. How tall at the shore? 4.4 m tall by the time the water is 10 m deep.
One slit makes a fan. What do two slits 10 cm apart make? 7 bright bands, with dark water between.
950 cars, 1,000 spaces. How far do the last cars go? Roll forward 81 spots per car, random retry 12.
Push a heavy block into a light one. How many clicks? 100 to 1: 31. 10,000 to 1: 314. Digits of pi.
Start level with the top of the loop. Does the puck make it round? No: it lets go 48 degrees short.
Let go of a stick and a ball. Which hits the table first? At 30 degrees the stick, ball 11 cm up.
Same pendulum, bigger swing. Does it take longer? Yes: 2.0 s a swing at 10 degrees, 2.5 s at 103.
Three holes in a full tank. Which jet lands farthest? The middle: 1.00 m. Top and bottom: 0.87 m.
The string gets shorter. Does the puck speed up? Through a hole: yes, 2 m/s. On a pole: no, 1 m/s
A ball dropped on a slope. How far apart does it land? 40, 80, 120, 160 cm apart: exactly 1:2:3:4
Twice the speed. How much farther to stop? Four times: 12.3 m from 50 km/h, 49.2 m from 100 km/h
Straight to the swimmer, or run farther first? Run farther first: 24.5 s. Straight line: 28.3 s
Bounce it up and down. Does it start to swing? 2 bounces a swing: yes, 11.4 deg. 1.5: no, 0.14 deg
How many bounces before it stops? More than the counter shows. 80%: at rest by 4.06 s, 90%: 8.58 s
Same speed, same finish. Does the dip slow it down? No: dip ball 1.56 s, flat ball 2.00 s
Sticky ball or bouncy ball: which block swings higher? The bouncy ball: 67 cm against 17 cm
Throw a bouncy ball under a table. So where does it go? Back to your hand, 97% of its forward speed
Merry-go-round: do you hit your friend? No, the ball misses by 2.0 m at 10 rpm
Which way does the spool roll? Axle half the wheel: toward the hand below 60 degrees, away above
Hit a ball dead on at 2 m/s: does the cue ball stop? No spin: dead stop. Rolling: 2/7 of its speed
Bucket over your head: how slow before it spills? 30 turns a minute on a 1 m arm
Drop a folded chain beside a ball, 1 m: which lands first? The chain, the ball still 28 cm up
Rope swing: when should you let go to fly farthest? 31 deg past the bottom, 10.26 m against 6 m
Lowered or dropped: how far does the spring squash? 5 cm lowered, 10 cm dropped, exactly double
Cut the ball: do the two balls split at a right angle? No spin: 90 degrees. Rolling: 63.7 degrees
Coin around a coin: how many times does it turn? 2 turns around, 1 turn along a flat strip
Pull the tablecloth: how fast must you pull? Above 1.1 m/s: 1 m/s rides off, 3 m/s moves 1.6 cm
Head-on at 50: same as a wall at 100? No. 44 cm of crush each, like a wall at 50. At 100: 88 cm
Stick on ice: where does the tip land? 41 cm on ice, 83 cm pinned in a hinge, exactly half
Will the ball swing round the peg? Halfway down: no, slack 48 deg short. 70 % down: yes. Needs 3/5
Wall ahead. Brake or swerve? Braking needs 12.3 m, a full swerve 24.6 m, twice as far
Which climbs higher, ice cube or ball? The ball, 64 cm against 46, 1.4 times as high
Hit it low at 2 m/s: does the cue ball come back? Only if the other ball is closer than 76.5 cm
Which one comes back, the ball or the ring? The ball, at 3/7 of its speed; the ring stops dead
Which rides along, the box or the ball? The box, at belt speed; the ball crawls at 2/7 of it
Which way does the balloon lean when the car speeds up? Forward, 15.8 degrees, the dice 15.8 back
Will the chain slide off the desk? 18 cm holds, 22 cm is gone in 1.25 s. The line: 20 cm, one fifth
Can two kilos hold twenty kilos? One turn round a post slips; two turns hold 86 kg
Does the car leave the road? 40 km/h no, 60 km/h yes: 16 m in the air; the limit is 49.7 km/h
Pull slowly or jerk it. Which string snaps? Slow: the top at 0.217 s. Jerked: the bottom at 0.005 s
Which is easier to balance, a pencil or a broom? Broom flat at 1.50 s, pencil 0.53 s, 2.83x: root 8
Where is the sweet spot on a bat? Hit 2/3 along: handle end 0.00 m/s. Hit the tip: 8.8 m/s back
Does the coin stay on the record? At 45 rpm it stays; at 78 rpm it is off the rim in 0.18 s
Aim at the flag, or aim upstream? Aim upstream: 83 s. Aim at the flag: 139 s, nearly twice as long
Drop a yo-yo beside a ball. Which lands first? The ball at 0.45 s; the yo-yo 1.97 s, 4.36x later
Two 1.1 kg weights. Which lands first? Dropped: 0.45 s. On a pulley vs 1.0 kg: 2.07 s, 4.6x later
Roll a ball at a 3 cm step. Does it get up? 0.7 m/s: no, 0.9 m/s: yes. The limit is 0.81 m/s
Carry a weight, then stop. Does it swing? Stop at 1 s: 18.4 degrees; stop at 2 s: it hangs still
Bolted down or free on ice: which block reaches the floor first? Free wedge 0.39 s, bolted 0.49 s
Which comes first, dry bottom or spill? 4 cm of water: dry at 342 rpm. 6 cm: spills at 342 rpm
Fired straight up from a rolling cart: does the ball land back in the cup? No, 43 cm behind it
Push down on a crate, or pull up on it: which one moves it? Pull up: 2.8 m in 2 s, push down: 0 m
Two rails or a flat board: which one gets down first? The flat board, 0.91 s against 1.12 s
Where do two fingers meet under a ruler? At the balance point: 50 cm, and 20 cm under a hammer
Marble or dice on a tilting tray: which one goes first? The marble at 5.6 deg, the dice at 26.7 deg
Does it matter if the boat is tied when you jump to the dock? Tied 1.25 m on the dock, free 0.52 m
Flat road or banked road: which one keeps the car in its lane? Banked holds; flat is off in 1.59 s
